title: High-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation for post-stroke cognitive impairment: A triple-blind randomized trial
title_zh: 高强度经颅交流电刺激治疗卒中后认知障碍：一项三盲随机试验
abstract: BACKGROUND: Non-invasive neuromodulation for post-stroke cognitive impairment (PSCI) holds promise, but high-level evidence is lacking, partly due to the challenge of targeting single brain regions in a condition with diverse lesions and multi-network dysfunction. OBJECTIVE: The present study aimed to evaluate the effect of high-intensity transcranial alternating current stimulation (Hi-tACS) on cognitive function in patients with PSCI. METHODS: In this triple-blind, randomized, sham-controlled trial, PSCI patients were randomized to receive either active or sham Hi-tACS. The tACS group received active Hi-tACS at 15 mA and 77.5 Hz for 40 min, twice daily, 5 days a week for 2 weeks. The sham group used identical devices without current delivery. The primary outcome was the change in Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) score. Secondary outcomes included Digit Span Test and cerebral oxyhemoglobin (HbO) concentration changes measured by functional near-infrared spectroscopy (fNIRS). RESULTS: The tACS group (n = 34) showed higher MoCA response rates than the sham group (n = 34) immediately after treatment (73.5% vs 38.2%, P = 0.003) and at the 4-week post-treatment follow-up (88.2% vs 55.9%, P = 0.003). Improvements in forward and backward digit span were also greater in the tACS group at both assessments. The intention-to-treat analysis of all 70 randomized participants yielded results consistent with the per-protocol analysis. Exploratory fNIRS analyses identified greater HbO increases in the left, right, and medial prefrontal regions in the tACS group at T1 after FDR correction (all q = 0.033), whereas no regional difference remained significant at T2. CONCLUSION: Hi-tACS improved global cognition and working memory in patients with PSCI and was generally well tolerated. Exploratory fNIRS findings suggested possible accompanying changes in cortical activation and network organization but did not establish a neurophysiological mechanism. Importantly, as a broad-network stimulation approach, Hi-tACS may reduce reliance on selecting a single precise target, a potential practical advantage in heterogeneous PSCI.
abstract_zh: 背景：非侵入性神经调控在治疗卒中后认知障碍（PSCI）方面具有潜力，但仍缺乏高级别证据。部分原因在于，PSCI患者的病灶多样，并存在多个脑网络的功能障碍，因此难以选择单一脑区作为刺激靶点。目的：本研究旨在评估高强度经颅交流电刺激（Hi-tACS）对PSCI患者认知功能的影响。方法：本研究采用三盲、随机、假刺激对照设计，将PSCI患者随机分配接受真实Hi-tACS或假刺激。tACS组接受电流强度15 mA、频率77.5 Hz的真实Hi-tACS，每次40分钟，每日两次，每周5天，持续2周。假刺激组使用相同设备，但不输送电流。主要结局为蒙特利尔认知评估量表（MoCA）评分的变化。次要结局包括数字广度测验，以及采用功能性近红外光谱（fNIRS）测量的脑氧合血红蛋白（HbO）浓度变化。结果：治疗结束即刻，tACS组（n=34）的MoCA应答率高于假刺激组（n=34）（73.5%比38.2%，P=0.003）；治疗结束后4周随访时亦如此（88.2%比55.9%，P=0.003）。两个评估时间点上，tACS组顺背和倒背数字广度的改善也均更大。针对全部70名随机入组参与者的意向性治疗分析与符合方案分析结果一致。探索性fNIRS分析发现，经FDR校正后，T1时点tACS组左侧、右侧及内侧前额叶区域的HbO增加幅度更大（所有q=0.033）；而T2时点各区域差异均不再显著。结论：Hi-tACS改善了PSCI患者的整体认知和工作记忆，且总体耐受性良好。探索性fNIRS结果提示，可能伴随皮层激活和网络组织的变化，但尚未确立神经生理机制。作为一种广泛作用于脑网络的刺激方式，Hi-tACS可能减少对选择单一精确靶点的依赖，这在异质性较高的PSCI中可能具有实际优势。
